trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth on US-2, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and follow it west to Eightmile Campground.
approach: From Eightmile Campground walk a few hundred feet west along Icicle Creek Road, away from town, then turn right and climb the slope to the buttress.
note: MP Eightmile Buttress Ice area page (Getting There) agreeing with MP Eight Mile Area and the route page location; no route-specific detail beyond that.
MP area and route pages give only 'left side of US-97 going north past the Chelan airport' and say safe legal parking must be found; no parking spot or walk named.

trailheadDirection: From Seattle take I-90 east to Exit 54 for Hyak, turn right onto WA-906 and keep on it past an immediate left, then after about 0.4 miles turn right into the Hyak Sno-Park (winter parking needs a daily fee or seasonal Sno-Park permit).
approach: From Hyak Sno-Park follow the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail (Iron Horse Trail) south for 3 miles, using the side snowshoe track if on snowshoes. Just before an information board on the left, find a narrow gully on the right, go down beside the creek from the culvert past two short ice steps, and bushwhack through downed trees to the falls, about 50 m off the trail.
note: MP Keechelus Lake Ice area page (Getting There) plus WTA Hyak Sno-Park driving directions; MP Keechelus Lake area places routes about 3.5 miles east of Hyak on the same trail.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 Exit 38 drive up the forest road system on Forest Road 9020 to the junction with Forest Road 9021, as far as snow allows (the usual winter way, instead of the summer trailhead at Exit 42).
approach: From the Forest Road 9021 junction walk the road about a mile, turn hard left onto spur 110, and a quarter mile before its hairpin leave the road and go up through the woods onto the open slope below the north bowl. Traverse along the base of that slope to directly beneath the couloir.
note: Two agreeing winter trip reports (Exit 38 / forest road approach to the entrance of the couloir); MP route page gives only the Exit 42 winter pull-off and no walk to the couloir. Road snow level decides how far a car gets.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 take Exit 47 for Denny Creek, cross the freeway and follow Forest Road 58 to the Denny Creek parking lots just past the campground (Northwest Forest Pass or Sno-Park permit).
approach: From the Denny Creek parking lots take the Melakwa Lake trail past Denny Creek up to Upper Melakwa Lake. From the lake go up the valley with the flows on your left, climbing steep firm snow in winter, under 30 minutes to the base of the Line of Fire cliff band on the northwest side of the lake.
note: MP Melakwa Flows area page (Melakwa Lake trail, flows up valley on the left) + trip report placing Line of Fire NW of Upper Melakwa Lake, under 30 min from camp; WTA for the drive.
Northwest Couloir is reached by glacier travel (White Salmon / Hanging Glacier) from the Baker ski area as a ski objective; no fetched page describes a walk to its base.
Mowich Lake road closed at Fairfax Bridge (SR 165) per NPS Oct 29 2026; no other public approach found, so no usable walk-in.

trailhead: Pacific Crest Trail crossing on Forest Road 9070
trailheadDirection: From I-90 take Exit 54 for Hyak and follow Hyak Dr NE; the pavement ends after 0.6 miles and the road becomes Forest Road 9070, which you follow 4.7 miles to the Pacific Crest Trail crossing.
approach: From the Pacific Crest Trail crossing on Forest Road 9070 follow the Pacific Crest Trail south for 1.7 miles to a cairned side trail that turns back uphill; it climbs to Abiel Pass and then to the crest of the South Spur.
note: WTA and MP describe only the hiking South Spur (PCT south then side trail); Northeast Route and Northwest Ridge start elsewhere (Annette Lake / Hyak), so the entry fits one of three routes. Low: not written.

trailhead: Forest Road 1202 off Tieton Reservoir Road
trailheadDirection: From Morton take US-12 to Rimrock Lake, turn right onto Tieton Reservoir Road and after a couple of miles turn left onto Forest Road 1202 (or 570 if snow dictates), going as far as your vehicle allows.
approach: From wherever Forest Road 1202 off Tieton Reservoir Road stops, improvise a line up to the northwest-facing cliff band, using old roads and trails where they help; with skis the bushwhack took over three hours.
note: MP Strobach Mountain Ice area page only: road choice depends on snow and the walk is improvised over 3+ hours; no fixed parking or path. Low: not written.
Entry is a brush station, not a climb; no access page found.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 Exit 38 follow SE Homestead Valley Road to Forest Road 9020, just before the road passes under the freeway, and drive about 0.2 miles to a pullout on the right at an old abandoned road.
approach: From the Forest Road 9020 pullout follow the old road south, then west toward the scree field under the wall; it is overgrown now, so expect some bushwhacking. At the scree stay on the road line to a small cut log, then turn uphill on a faint trail to the crag base, roughly 0.2 miles and under 20 minutes.
note: MP Black Ice Crag Drytooling Park approach + trip report on CYA at Black Ice Crag (0.2 mile adventurous approach, old road overgrown); assumes Upper Black Ice is the ice wall over that crag.

trailheadDirection: From Enumclaw drive SR 410 east toward Crystal Mountain to the signed Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout on the right, about 9.5 miles south of Greenwater.
approach: From the Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout cross the White River, the hardest part of the day; how you cross changes year to year. Then scramble the steep, soft slope up to the base of the falls.
note: MP Skookum Falls route page (pullout, crossing the river) + Northwest Waterfall Survey (viewpoint on SR 410, 9.5 miles south of Greenwater) + MP area page (SR 410 from Enumclaw) + visitrainier (steep soft scramble to base).

trailheadDirection: From White Pass drive east on US-12 for about 2.2 miles to the Dog Lake parking area; the Clear Creek Falls overlook lot itself is often snowed in.
approach: From the Dog Lake parking area walk about 10 minutes, with some bushwhacking, to the overlook above the falls, and drop to the creek above the lip. The falls are usually top-roped or rappelled from there, so the base is reached from above; use snowshoes in deep snow.
note: MP Clear Creek Falls route page (park near Dog Lake, 10 min with bushwhacking) + climber.org 2004 report (Dog Lake outlet 2.2 miles east of White Pass, snow hike to the top of the falls).
Only an AAJ write-up of the route (skied around to the west face of Chair Peak); no parking or walk described.
